title: Establish roving-tabindex strategy and perceptual color ramp for micro-interactions in compact data grids
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: define and ship a roving-tabindex pattern and a perceptually-tuned color ramp for micro-interactions (row hover, row focus, inline actions, pill filters) inside compact data grids and dense tables. Scope: compact-density tables, virtualized lists used in Insights dashboards, table row action pills, filter chips, and inline editable cells. Out of scope for this ticket: chart color ramps (separate ticket), full theming API changes.

Why now: Several customer reports and internal UX audits show inconsistent keyboard traversal inside compact grids (tabbing jumps to last tabbable element, arrow-key expectations not met) and contrast failures when dense tokens sit on muted backgrounds. This causes regressions in screen reader flow and reduces usability for keyboard-only users.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented roving-tabindex implementation pattern for dense tables that supports arrow-key navigation, Home/End behavior, Shift+Tab reverse traversal, and predictable tab stop behavior for embedded interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs).
- Updated token mappings for focus outline and hover states with contrast ratios meeting WCAG AA for normal text (minimum 4.5:1 where applicable) and 3:1 for UI components per our accessibility policy. Provide numeric samples (e.g., focus ring #0A3B66 on bg #FFFFFF = 7.2:1; muted pill text #505F6B on pill bg #E8EDF2 = 4.7:1).
- Figma component variants and a short usage guide (2–3 screenshots) added to the Design System file.
- A small end-to-end a11y test harness (Jest + Playwright axe) demonstrating keyboard traversal scenarios and automated contrast checks for the tokens.
- A VPAT evidence snippet describing how the pattern maps to ATAG/ARIA expectations and keyboard operability (to be used by PM/support).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We adopt a roving-tabindex approach (single tabindex=0, others -1) rather than complex focus-skip heuristics to keep runtime overhead low and behaviors deterministic across virtualized lists.
- For rows that contain multiple controls (e.g., inline edit + primary action), Tab should move into a row-level toolbar and arrow keys should navigate between cells; this preserves expected spreadsheet-like behavior for power users at the cost of slightly deeper focus trees.
- We will keep the visual focus token strong (outline thickness and contrast) even in compact density to avoid hidden focus in small touch targets. This slightly increases visual noise but improves discoverability.

Implementation notes for engineering:
- Provide a small TypeScript utility with a simple API: initRoving(containerEl, options) -> handles keydown for ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down, Home, End, Tab/Shift+Tab. The utility will expose programmatic focusNext()/focusPrev() for programmatic actions.
- Use data-focusable attributes to identify navigation targets inside virtualized rows (so rendering frameworks can mark elements without coupling to specifics).
- Ensure compatibility with React Fiber-based virtualization (e.g., react-window) by avoiding reliance on DOM order for focus logic; use index-based mapping and visible index translation.

Testing plan:
- Manual test matrix: keyboard-only traversal, screen reader linearization (NVDA/VoiceOver), high-contrast theme check, zoom at 200%, and mobile keyboard navigation (for table uses on tablet contexts).
- Automated tests: Playwright flows that assert activeElement after Arrow keystrokes. Axe runs for contrast on rendered tokens.

Artifacts & links:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/DS-compact-grids-a11y
- Spec doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/980999/Roving+Tabindex+and+Color+Ramp+Spec
- Implementation stub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-ui/pull/2448
- Test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/a11y-tests/tree/main/compact-grid

Rollout plan:
1) Merge token updates and roving utility to canary branch of design-system package.
2) Ship to internal apps behind feature flag for Insights and Console beta users.
3) Collect telemetry for keyboard usage and any regression in click/hover metrics for 2 weeks.
4) Iterate before full release; create follow-up tickets for chart ramp alignment and theming API if needed.

Notes for VPAT/Compliance:
- Include a short evidence section showing keyboard operability scenarios and contrast measurement screenshots. This ticket will produce the evidence snippet; final VPAT update will live in the compliance repo (managed by Security/Compliance team).

Open questions:
- Should arrow-key behavior be configurable per-table (simple vs spreadsheet mode)? Proposal: default to simple for lists, spreadsheet-mode opt-in via data attribute.
- Do we need explicit support for nested focusable regions (expandable rows)? We'll handle basic cases; complex nested grids are deferred.

Next steps:
- Design review scheduled 2025-03-04. Action: Omar to post Figma prototypes and token samples by 2025-03-03.
- ENG ticket dependency: ENG-55420 (virtualized-list focus stability) must land or be coordinated with this rollout.
